title: Augmented Koszul scalar extension and its quotient square
statement: Let $A,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to S$ a ring homomorphism, $r\geq0$, and $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in A$ any sequence. Put $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ and $I_S=(\varphi(g_1),\ldots,\varphi(g_r))$. Use the Koszul complexes $K_A(g)$ and $K_S(\varphi g)$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], placed in cochain degrees $-q$, and their quotient augmentations $\epsilon_A:K_A(g)\to(A/I)[0]$ and $\epsilon_S:K_S(\varphi g)\to(S/I_S)[0]$, quotient in degree zero and zero in other degrees. Put $F(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_A S[0])$ with its $S$-action [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor], and let $Q_S$ be localization to $D(S)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The balanced map $$\theta:(A/I)\otimes_A S\xrightarrow{\sim}S/I_S,\qquad\bar a\otimes s\longmapsto\overline{\varphi(a)s},$$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism with inverse $\bar s\mapsto\bar1\otimes s$. There is an isomorphism $$\beta:Q_SF(K_A(g))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(K_S(\varphi g))$$ in $D(S)$, represented by the cochain isomorphism sending $(e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_q})\otimes s$ to $s(e_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge e_{i_q})$, with the usual degree-zero tensor unit identification. These maps satisfy $$Q_S(\theta[0])\circ Q_S(F(\epsilon_A))=Q_S(\epsilon_S)\circ\beta,$$ where $F((A/I)[0])$ is canonically $((A/I)\otimes_A S)[0]$. No flatness or regularity is assumed, and empty sequences and zero rings are included.

source.place: Tag 062H (lemma-koszul-regular-flat-base-change), first identity in its proof, together with definition-koszul-complex and its differential formula; augmentation compatibility is the explicit wedge and balanced-quotient calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] with $B=S$ and $I=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$: its extended ideal is $I_S$, and its inverse sends $s\otimes\bar a$ to $\overline{\varphi(a)s}$. Flip the factors by $\bar a\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes\bar a$, whose inverse is the same flip; both respect the balancing relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the $S$-actions. Composing gives exactly $\theta$ and its inverse $\bar s\mapsto\bar1\otimes s$.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), quotient specialization; explicit balanced formulas of the cited tensor-quotient node.

proof.text: Apply [def-pc-mixed-total-tensor] with base ring $A$, output ring $S$, first complex $S[0]$, and second complex $E$. Only the summand with first degree $0$ remains, so its degree-$n$ term is $S\otimes_A E^n$ and its differential is $1\otimes d_E$, with sign $(-1)^0=1$. The factor flip $s\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes s$ and its inverse respect balancing and identify this complex with $F(E)$, with $S$ acting on the second factor and differential $d_E\otimes1$. The same formula commutes with maps of $E$. Thus $F((A/I)[0])$ is canonically $((A/I)\otimes_A S)[0]$.

source.place: Tag 062H (lemma-koszul-regular-flat-base-change), first complex identification; totalization specialized to a degree-zero second factor.

proof.text: For each $q\geq0$ write $e_J^A,e_J^S$ for the ordered $q$-fold standard basis wedges, indexed by $q$-element subsets $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. If $x=\sum_J a_J e_J^A$, define $b_q(x\otimes s)=\sum_J\varphi(a_J)s e_J^S$. This is balanced and defines a map on the tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Define $c_q(\sum_J s_J e_J^S)=\sum_J e_J^A\otimes s_J$. Both maps are $S$-linear; $b_qc_q=1$ by the displayed coordinates, while $c_qb_q(x\otimes s)=\sum_J e_J^A\otimes\varphi(a_J)s=x\otimes s$ by balancing. Thus they are inverse. For $q=0$ this is $A\otimes_A S\to S$, $a\otimes s\mapsto\varphi(a)s$; for $q>r$ both modules are zero.

source.place: Tags 0622 (definition-koszul) and 0623 (definition-koszul-complex), standard exterior terms; explicit basis-coordinate construction of the first identity in Tag 062H.

proof.text: For $J=(i_1<\cdots<i_q)$ the differential formula in [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] gives $d_A(e_J^A)=\sum_{k=1}^q(-1)^{k-1}g_{i_k}e_{J\setminus i_k}^A$. Hence $b_{q-1}((d_Ae_J^A)\otimes s)=\sum_k(-1)^{k-1}\varphi(g_{i_k})s e_{J\setminus i_k}^S=d_S(se_J^S)$. Linearity and tensor generation give this identity on every element. In degree $0$ both outgoing differentials are zero. Place $b_q$ in cochain degree $-q$ and zero in positive degrees. These inverse component maps therefore form a cochain isomorphism $b:F(K_A(g))\xrightarrow{\sim}K_S(\varphi g)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The inverse commutes with differentials too: multiplying $b_{q-1}(d_A\otimes1)=d_Sb_q$ on the left by $c_{q-1}$ and on the right by $c_q$ gives $(d_A\otimes1)c_q=c_{q-1}d_S$.

source.place: Tag 0622 (definition-koszul), displayed differential formula immediately following the definition; first identity in Tag 062H.

proof.text: The stated augmentations are cochain maps: their only possibly nonzero composite with an incoming differential sends $e_i$ to the class of $g_i$, respectively $\varphi(g_i)$, which is zero [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. In degree zero, both $\theta[0]\circ F(\epsilon_A)$ and $\epsilon_S\circ b$ send $a\otimes s$ to $\overline{\varphi(a)s}$. In every other degree their target is zero. Tensor generation [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] proves equality of these cochain maps.

source.place: Tags 0622 and 0623, degree-one differential and degree-zero quotient augmentation; explicit augmentation-square calculation.

proof.text: Apply the localization functor $Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $b$ and its inverse: their composites still give the identities, so $\beta=Q_S(b)$ is an isomorphism. Functoriality applied to the equality in the preceding step gives exactly the claimed equation. When $r=0$, the only basis wedge is $1$, $I=I_S=0$, and all maps reduce to the tensor unit and quotient identifications above. Zero rings cause no exception: the displayed inverse and differential identities remain valid, including when the tensor modules are zero. No step used exactness of scalar extension or regularity.

source.place: Tag 062H, first identity in its proof; elementary functorial passage from the augmented cochain isomorphism to the derived category.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0622/0623 and the first identity in the proof of Tag 062H; explicit coordinate and augmentation calculations supplied by Q149.
